title: A day of local food in the Roaring Fork Valley
lede: From the valley's first homestead to a Michelin-starred dinner: a ranch walk, a farm-shop lunch, a ride up Maroon Creek, and kitchens that name the farms on your plate.
route: Carbondale → Basalt → Aspen, about 45 minutes of driving in all (Hwy 82). The evening has an up-valley and a down-valley option.

inspired.label: Roaring Fork + Farm Map
inspired.note: The valley tourism boards' guide to local food champions, farms and visitor ranches. Plan built 2026-10-04.

stops.title: Start where valley farming began
stops.why: An 1885 homestead kept with the Thompson family's own furniture and belongings. The Roaring Fork + Farm Map calls it the starting point for any farm visit.
stops.tip: Tours are by appointment only. Book through the historical society before you go.

stops.title: Walk a working regenerative ranch
stops.why: A 113-acre regenerative-agriculture and education ranch between Carbondale and Basalt, with farm tours and hayrides. Its vegetables turn up at Element 47.
stops.tip: Open Wed–Fri 9am–4pm, plus Saturday mornings in summer.

alt.why: On a Friday morning, pick your own at the Basalt farm whose vegetables supply Bosq.

stops.title: Lunch at a farmhouse kitchen

place.node: Meat & Cheese Restaurant and Farm Shop

stops.why: Aspen's farm-shop restaurant: local eggs, produce and cheese at the counter, Mesa Microgreens from Silt on the plate.
stops.tip: Hours change with the season, and it closes in November. Check before you go.

stops.title: Get out on the ranch
stops.why: A family ranch on Maroon Creek Road since 1938. Maroon Bells Outfitters runs its summer trail rides.

alt.why: Prefer to stay on foot? Visit the nonprofit farm at Cozy Point Ranch for classes, tours and the farm market.

stops.title: Dinner up valley
stops.why: Barclay Dodge's Michelin-starred kitchen, cooking with Two Roots Farm vegetables and Mesa Microgreens.

alt.why: The Little Nell's dining room publishes its full purveyor list, from Rock Bottom Ranch vegetables to Cross Creek Farms Wagyu.

stops.title: Head back down valley for the evening
stops.why: Stop for a tasting in Basalt. Nearly everything in the bottle is grown in Colorado, and its apple brandy goes into Il Porcellino's salami.

alt.why: Carbondale's distillery runs on grain grown less than a mile away by partners like Nieslanik Beef.
Seasonal dinner in Glenwood Springs, with Mesa Microgreens from just down the road.
On a summer Thursday, finish at the rodeo in Carbondale.

stops.label: Or, down valley

pantry.title: Take the valley home
pantry.why: Pick up local meat and eggs before you leave.

title: A day of local food in Chaffee County
lede: Saturday market in Salida, a self-serve garlic farm stand, a 150-year-old homestead, lunch in Buena Vista on beef raised at 8,000 feet, a goat creamery, and dinner back in Salida.
best: Saturday, June–October (the Salida Farmers Market season)
route: Salida → Buena Vista → Salida on US-285 and US-24, about 60 miles of driving in all.

inspired.label: Chaffee Provides
inspired.note: Envision Chaffee County and Guidestone's local food map, plus the farms' own sites and local press. Chaffee has no tourism-board farm map, so this plan was researched directly on 2026-10-04.

stops.title: Start at the Saturday market
stops.why: Two acres of farm stands in Alpine Park, a block from downtown. The Triangle Oasis hands out its CSA shares here.
stops.tip: 8am–noon through Sept 11, then 9am–noon to Oct 24. Accepts SNAP and Double Up Food Bucks.

place.listing: Market on Main St. (The Triangle Oasis)

alt.why: Off-season or off a Saturday? The Triangle Oasis's downtown store sells its produce and flowers plus locally made goods.

stops.title: Fill a bag at a garlic farm
stops.why: A Certified Naturally Grown market garden known for hardneck garlic, with a self-serve farm stand. Its spring thyme went into Mantis Kitchen's syrups.
stops.tip: Self-serve, May–November. Bring cash, a check or Venmo. Scanga Meat Company is next door.

stops.title: Step back 150 years on a working homestead
stops.why: Guidestone runs the Hutchinson Homestead & Learning Center on the 1867 Hutchinson family homestead. It hosts heritage tours, summer farm brunches and October's pumpkin patch.
stops.tip: Opening varies by event. Check Guidestone's calendar before you drive out.

stops.title: Lunch on Arrowpoint beef in Buena Vista
stops.why: A wood-fired kitchen whose beef is grass-fed Highland cattle from Arrowpoint Cattle Company, raised at 8,000 feet outside Nathrop.

stops.title: Meet the goats
stops.why: A creamery at the BV Farm General Store, making goat and cow cheeses (chèvre, feta, bloomy rinds, cave-aged) where Jumpin' Good Goat Dairy used to be.
stops.tip: The self-serve store is open daily. Public farm tours run Saturdays at 10am; sign up online, and start the day in Buena Vista if you want the tour.

alt.why: Buena Vista's natural grocer stocks Headwater Farms produce year round.

stops.title: Dinner back in Salida
stops.why: Salida's new Italian trattoria, from the team behind Shavano, cooks with produce and beef from Hutchinson Ranch.
stops.tip: New in 2026. Check hours and book ahead.

stops.label: Or, stay on the farm
stops.title: Spend the night with the goats
stops.why: A goat-farm B&B six miles out of Salida, with cheesemaking, goat-care and poultry classes. Farm tours are free for guests.

pantry.title: Take Chaffee home
pantry.why: Local beef and produce to pack in the cooler.
